message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on "Desert Atlas" stone. The lab found an igneous stone with almost no quartz, which is not granite, and CBP likely classified it as "other" under heading 6802 as worked monumental or building stone. Heading 6802 covers worked monumental or building stone, and subheading 6802.91 and following cover other stone: 6802.91 marble, travertine, alabaster; 6802.92 other calcareous stone; 6802.93 granite; 6802.99 other stone.

The product is a slab with a honed top and sawn sides, so it is worked beyond simple cutting. Heading 6802 covers stone that is further worked, for example honed or polished, while sawn-only slabs fall under 2515 or 2516.

Because the top is honed, the slab falls under 6802. Since the stone is igneous with almost no quartz, it is not "granite" in the commercial sense, so 6802.93 is out. Under 6802.99, "other stone", the slab is 3 cm thick. The statistical suffixes are 6802.99.0040 for other, thickness 10 cm or more, and 6802.99.0060 for other.

Checking the 6802.99 breakdown: 6802.99.00 is "Other", with 6802.99.0010 for "Slabs, tiles... of thickness ... " I do not recall this breakdown precisely. I believe the suffixes are 6802.99.0020 for "Other: Of other stone," 6802.99.0040 for "Other" and 6802.99.0060 for other. I will go with 6802.99.0060.
